title: Runtime scheduler: separate prefill vs decode scheduling hooks to avoid long-prefill dominating batch selection
author: Omar El-Sayed
description:
Context: Mixed prompt-length distributions (short chat prompts interleaved with long-context prompts) expose head-of-line blocking in our current continuous batching path. One recurring contributor is that the scheduler’s single “next batch” selection path conflates prefill and decode work, so a long prefill can repeatedly win selection and starve latency-sensitive decode/short-prefill traffic.

This PR refactors scheduler hooks to cleanly separate prefill and decode scheduling decisions, without changing the external API surface. The goal is to enable the upcoming class-based/two-queue policy (ENG-2438) to independently decide how much prefill vs decode to admit per iteration and to prevent long-prefill from dominating batch selection.

What changed (high level): 1) Split the scheduler entrypoints into stage-aware hooks: build_prefill_batch(...) and build_decode_batch(...). The previous build_next_batch(...) is kept as a thin adapter for legacy policies and tests, but it no longer owns policy decisions. 2) Introduce explicit “WorkItem” stage tagging (PREFILL/DECODE) and a stable ordering contract: within a stage, we keep FIFO ordering per queue; across stages the policy decides (no implicit prefill-first behavior). 3) Move KV-cache reservation/validation to the boundary between selection and dispatch: prefill selection now performs reservation checks earlier to avoid selecting items that cannot be dispatched due to cache pressure; decode selection keeps the existing fast-path. 4) Add a lightweight stage-local accounting struct (PrefillIterationStats / DecodeIterationStats) to make it easy to attribute time-in-queue, TTFT, and selection share in the follow-up metrics PR.

Why this helps: By making prefill and decode separate scheduling decisions, the two-queue policy can (a) prioritize short-prefill for TTFT while still (b) ensuring decode progress for in-flight sequences, and (c) cap long-prefill dominance by applying per-stage/per-class budgets (added in a follow-up PR).

Notes on behavior changes: - Default/legacy policy behavior should be unchanged for homogeneous workloads. - Under mixed workloads, we should see fewer cases where a single large prefill repeatedly fills the batch while ready-to-decode sequences wait behind it. - This PR does not yet implement token budgets / class-based dispatch; it only creates the hooks and moves stage-specific invariants to the right place.

Test plan: - Added unit tests for stage separation invariants (prefill does not consume decode-ready slots; decode batch builder ignores prefill-only items). - Expanded scheduler regression tests to exercise “long prefill + many decode-ready” and assert bounded decode wait. - Ran benchmark-lab local smoke (mixed 80/20 short/long) on A100-80GB: no throughput regression observed in the smoke run; TTFT improved in the worst-case synthetic case (see perf notes below).

Perf notes (local smoke, single node): - Baseline vs this PR (no two-queue policy yet): p95 TTFT improved ~6–11% on the synthetic ‘long-prefill spike’ case due to fewer decode stalls; throughput within noise (<1%). Full results will be captured once the class policy lands.

Rollout: No runtime config changes. This is a refactor gated by tests; the follow-up policy PR will be behind a feature flag.

Related: - PR #24844 (two-queue dispatch policy) will consume the new hooks. - PR #24831 (short/long classification) remains orthogonal. - Follow-up will add token-budget guardrails + metrics wiring.
commits: runtime/scheduler: introduce Stage enum and WorkItem tagging
runtime/scheduler: split build_next_batch into build_prefill_batch + build_decode_batch
runtime/kv: move kv reservation checks earlier for prefill selection
tests: add stage separation unit tests + mixed prefill/decode regression
cleanup: keep legacy adapter for build_next_batch to minimize churn
review_conversation: Lena Fischer (review): The hook split makes sense, but I want to ensure we don’t accidentally regress decode fairness for in-flight sequences. Can you document the new ordering contract and add a regression test that asserts decode-ready items can still be selected even when prefill queue is non-empty?

Omar El-Sayed (author): Added explicit ordering contract to scheduler_notes.md and added scheduler_mixed_prefill_decode_regression_test.cc covering ‘long prefill + many decode-ready’. The test asserts decode waits are bounded and that decode builder ignores prefill-only items.

Hiro Tanaka (review): Any risk this changes kernel auto-selection assumptions? Some of our prefill kernels expect stable batch shapes; separating stages might increase churn if we alternate too frequently.

Omar El-Sayed (author): This PR only separates hook boundaries; the legacy adapter still behaves prefill-first like before. The two-queue policy will control alternation; we’ll add guardrails there (min-stage-run / hysteresis). I added a note in scheduler_notes.md and will track kernel shape stability in the policy PR.

Sean Gallagher (review): From an ops perspective, we’ll need visibility once policy toggles. Can you at least plumb a stage-level counter now so we can confirm selection share doesn’t go pathological in canary?

Omar El-Sayed (author): Kept this PR refactor-only, but I added PrefillIterationStats/DecodeIterationStats structs so the next metrics PR can export consistent counters. The metrics wiring will land with #24888 to avoid half-measures.
Marcus Reed (review): Minor: please keep build_next_batch as an adapter for now to reduce rebase pain across policy branches; also add a comment about where KV reservation happens for prefill.
Omar El-Sayed (author): Done. build_next_batch now delegates to stage builders, and I added comments near the reservation boundary in kv_cache_manager.cc.
Lena Fischer (final): Approved once CI is green and the regression test is in. Looks good.
Hiro Tanaka (final): Approved. Please follow up on hysteresis when policy alternates stages.
Sean Gallagher (final): Approved. Make sure the canary runbook references the upcoming per-stage metrics once they exist.
release_notes: Internal refactor only: scheduler now has separate prefill/decode batch builders to support upcoming mixed-workload scheduling policy; no config changes.
